Subject: AcmeBank — region pinning & failover questions

Thanks for the time today, Jordan — really useful call. Quick recap and a few follow-ups so we can scope the region/residency work: 

Summary from call:
- AcmeBank needs EU data (customer personal data and derived embeddings) to remain in the EU for production workloads.
- You asked about cross-region failover and whether backups can be stored outside the EU.
- Desired: automated failover for availability, but legal/ops want proof that backups and long-term storage remain in-region unless explicitly permitted.

A few clarifying questions so we can put together a concrete proposal / MPA wording:
1) For "data must remain in EU": does that apply to backups and disaster recovery replicas, or only to live production data?
2) For cross-region failover: is temporary (during an outage) failover to a non-EU region acceptable if you have contractual guarantees that replicate data is transient and deleted after failover event? Or is any copy outside EU disallowed?
3) What RTO/RPO expectations do you have for the failover scenario? (This will drive whether we recommend synchronous replication vs async + warm standby.)

Next steps I propose: we'll put together a short technical note that outlines the region-pinning options (per-account region pinning, cross-region failover options, backup geo-location, and KMS options), and a draft MPA snippet. Can you confirm LegalOps (legal@acmebank.com) should be looped in on the next doc?

Attaching a short summary diagram of how region pinning typically looks in Redwood for reference.

Thanks — Marissa

- "Data must remain in the EU" applies to both production data and backups/replicas by default. Any deviation (e.g., temporary cross-region replication) would require prior written approval from our legal team.

- RTO target is 1 hour and RPO is 15 minutes for critical flows, but we understand that may require special config.

Subject: Re: AcmeBank — region pinning & failover questions

Appreciate the detail, Jordan — helpful. Quick notes from our side and what we'll include in the technical note: 

1) Region pinning: Redwood supports per-account region pinning. You can pin production model inference and embeddings storage to a specific region (e.g., eu-west-1).

2) Backups & replication: By default, snapshots/backups are stored in the primary pinned region. We support options to replicate backups to a secondary region for DR, but that replication is explicit per-account and requires configuration/approval.

3) Cross-region failover: We can support automated failover for availability. Options include:
   - Active-passive with async replication (lower latency impact, potential RPO > 15m)
   - Active-active (geo-replicated reads) — more complex and usually not allowed when strict residency is required.

4) Deletion/retention workflow: we can provide automated post-failover deletion hooks and audit logs showing when and what was deleted. We also support customer-managed KMS so keys never leave the EU.

Given your RTO/RPO targets, we'll recommend a configuration with encrypted async replication to a pre-approved DR region combined with warm standby capacity. If Legal requires no copies outside EU under any circumstance, we will instead recommend a Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or a cross-account EU-only standby. 

I'm attaching a short one-page summary and our proposed MPA language for region pinning and DR. Can LegalOps confirm whether temporary DR replication plus documented deletion workflow is acceptable?

Proposed next step: 30-min follow-up with Aditya (serving/runtime) and Sean (SRE) to walk technical options. Are you available Thurs or Fri this week?

Thanks — Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: AcmeBank — region pinning & failover questions

Thanks for the ping — here are the technical answers we can provide to Acme: 

- Per-account region pinning: Supported. We pin inference, embeddings storage, and default snapshot locations to the selected region (eu-west-1).

- Cross-region replication/failover:
  * Async replication to a pre-approved DR region is supported. Typical RPO for async replication depends on workload and batch window; with continuous streaming we can achieve ~5-15 minute RPOs under normal load.
  * Synchronous geo-replication to meet sub-15m RPOs is generally infeasible at long distances without significant latency impact; we recommend async + warm standby for the 15m RPO target and design for a 1h RTO with automated failover scripts.
  * Automated failover is configurable per account. We can mark cross-region replication as "disabled" by default and enable only with Legal/Customer approval.

- Backups & retention:
  * Snapshots/backups are stored in-region by default. Replication to a secondary region is explicit and audited.
  * We support customer-managed KMS keys scoped to EU to ensure keys do not leave region. Backups encrypted with CMK remain unreadable outside EU without key access.

- Deletion/audit workflow:
  * Post-failover deletion hooks can be executed automatically (server-side job) or triggered via API by the customer.
  * All deletion events are logged and surfaced in the Redwood Console (audit trail). We can provide proof-of-deletion artifacts for Legal.

Attachments: technical-note-region-pinning.md (technical note)

I'll join the follow-up call and can walk through RTO/RPO tradeoffs and the implementation plan. If Legal requires an absolute prohibition on any cross-region copy, we should discuss Private deployment or EU-only standby architectures.

— Aditya
